title.narrative: PERFORMANCE-BASED PARTNERSHIP SCHEME FOCUSING ON QUALITY PROGRAMMING, UNDERSTANDING CHANGE AND RESULTS FOR POOR HOUSEHOLDS AND COMMUNITIES

description.narrative: The Integrated Health and Nutrition programme will work in Northern Bahr el Ghazal, South Sudan. It aims to contribute to Concern South Sudan’s Health, Nutrition and WASH thematic programme, and the goal of the grant is to improve child and maternal health and nutritional status by increasing access to essential integrated health, nutrition services and promoting sustainable behaviour change. The programme will support over 634,484 people living in extreme and poor households with a particular focus on pregnant and lactating mothers, and children under five, female-headed households, pregnant and lactating mothers, households with disabled members. This will be done through increased availability and access to basic quality health/nutrition services and integration opportunities analysed jointly with the Ministry of Health/County Health Department and promoted, improved capacity of the health facility staff to provide comprehensive quality health and nutrition services, increased access to nutritive sensitive agriculture (vegetable production) and participation in VSLAs by vulnerable groups and increased engagement of women and men to promote positive gender roles at community and household level.. OVERALL COUNTRY PROG: Providing lifesaving and early recovery assistance to communities affected by chronic crisis in targeted areas in South Sudan.. SPECIFIC OUTCOME: Gender equality 2: this is the main objective of the outcome, which is aimed at as it focus on reducing barriers and increasing access of women to basic health and nutrition services. RM Adaptation 1: HHs receive basic technical training on climate-smart agricultural practices and the formulation of organic pesticides to control pests as wqell as on the application of manure to improve soil fertility. DRR 1: Through system strengthening, the programme is strengthening the resilience of the heath system.Capacity Building 1:RMNC Health 1: The aim of this programme is to improve child and maternal health and nutritional status by improving access to essential health, nutrition, water, sanitation and hygiene services and by promoting sustainable behaviour change for optimal feeding, caring and hygiene for children under-five and their carers. The primary target groups are children under-five and women of reproductive age, particularly pregnant women.Nutrition 1: Improving the nutrition status of women and children through improved nutrition awareness among communities is a focus of this outcome.
